decisions.rationale: All 197 comparators were reviewed in the reversed orientation. PF-0169 combines Revert and Rewind and adds shared recovery semantics, so it is an umbrella rather than the same single-command feature.

All 197 comparators were reviewed. PF-0169 is the combined Revert-and-Rewind recovery contract; its umbrella scope and additional failure semantics keep it distinct from the chat-only Rewind boundary.

PF-0172 describes the same YOLO auto-approval control, CSS-only lifecycle, missing authority boundary, user outcome, state boundary, and fail-safe gap. PF-0165 concerns projected bypass status and receipts, not the control itself. All 197 comparators were checked.

PF-0170 is the same composer attachment-chip removal feature with the same DOM-only lifecycle, trust boundary, retained-state uncertainty, and failure semantics. PF-0171 is the adjacent Attach File and agent-selection input flow. All 197 comparators were checked.

PF-0173 is a broader selector suite covering mode, role, model, and reasoning with compatibility and dispatch semantics. The model-and-effort member remains distinct under the umbrella/member rule. All 197 comparators were reviewed.

The listed comparators are separate fixture controls, bottom-panel state, or the general promotion gate. They share the non-evidence boundary but not one product lifecycle and state boundary. All 197 comparators were reviewed.

PF-0190 is the same terminal-button command-token feature with fixture-only authority, absent canonical binding, and identical evidentiary failure semantics. PF-0180 and PF-0182 cover different terminal steps or a broader terminal fixture set. All 197 comparators were checked.

Bottom-panel tabs and diagnostic rows or subtabs are plausible accessibility neighbors, but they are different controls with different interaction state and failure boundaries from terminal navigation chips and icons. All 197 comparators were reviewed.
PF-0191 is a nearby pointer-only diagnostics control family, but rows and subtabs do not share the info-icon product outcome or state boundary. No comparator among all 197 is merge-equivalent.

PF-0158 is another destructive, unwired action needing confirmation, receipts, rollback, and recovery, but thread archive has a different authority, lifecycle, and user outcome from the recovery-action family. All 197 comparators were reviewed.

Diagnostic rows and the fixture-only Show Problems control occupy the same Problems neighborhood, but neither is the footer interaction with its role and keyboard failure boundary. All 197 comparators were reviewed.

PF-0194 defines the promotion oracle for PMConcept controls, while this anchor allocates final GUI authority to named external owners. Related governance boundaries do not make their authority and outcomes identical. All 197 comparators were checked.

The promotion gate relies on canonical owners, but it is not the source-reference handoff record itself and has different lifecycle and validation semantics. Exhaustive review of 197 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature.

Thread, LSP, and remote-readiness projections are concrete neighbors of mock status truth, but each has its own state source, freshness lifecycle, and recovery behavior. All 197 comparators were reviewed and none matches the broad PMConcept mock-copy boundary.
Exhaustive review of all 197 comparators found no other feature whose product authority and lifecycle are the reconciliation source SHA identity record; superficial identity vocabulary was rejected.

The Rust/Tauri lineage ambiguity and the current Rust/Slint baseline are toolchain-authority neighbors, but neither is the explicit quarantine of stale fixture strings. All 197 comparators were reviewed.
PF-0178 quarantines one local-path fixture and is therefore a member of the broader sensitive-looking-values authority boundary, not a merge-equivalent feature. All 197 comparators were reviewed.

Terminal and settings contract gaps are members, and the PMConcept promotion gate is the adjacent governance rule. Their bounded authorities and outcomes differ from the broad negative-space inventory. All 197 comparators were reviewed.

Route normalization, identity, target navigation, and cross-surface navigation are plausible routing neighbors, but none combines the same graph host-pivot safety and shared deep-link payload boundary. All 197 comparators were reviewed.

The comparators address graph ownership, readability scale, or accessibility parity separately. The anchor uniquely joins quantitative large-graph limits with inspector disclosure policy, so umbrella/member and adjacency rules keep them distinct. All 197 were reviewed.

Context inspection/rewrite and Context Lens controls are neighboring context surfaces, but prompt compilation disclosure has different authority, data exposure, accessibility state, and failure semantics. All 197 comparators were checked.

All 197 comparators were exhaustively reviewed; none governs active-versus-focused historical run identity and focus-persistence conflict semantics. Generic projection or settings state was not treated as equivalent or a plausible feature neighbor.

Atomic GUI revalidation and canonical runtime-fact truth are adjacent trust mechanisms, but they do not own the run-graph projection trust gate, adjacent-owner adjudication, and behavioral oracle bundle. All 197 comparators were reviewed.
